quizName:
Hardest Questions in Florida
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if there were no construction.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and drive carefully when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Not obeying is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn across the median.
Stop on the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Get a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: To help prevent fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break to avoid fatigue. If you feel sleepy, pull over safely and take a nap or stay overnight.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other drivers are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and drive carefully when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive extra carefully in school zones.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Move your vehicle off the road and stop if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: When can you pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk?

options.text: When the vehicle doesn't speed up fast enough after the pedestrian leaves.
When the pedestrian is right in front of the vehicle.
When you don't see a pedestrian.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Florida law says you must assume any stopped vehicle at a crosswalk is waiting for a pedestrian, even if you cannot see one.

questions.question: If a gate near a drawbridge is about to lower across the road, you should:

options.text: Find a way around the gate.
Drive quickly under the lowering gate.
Stop completely and wait for the gate to rise.
Stop only if you cannot pass under the gate before it closes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait for the gate to rise.
questions.explanation: Many drawbridges have gates with flashing red lights and bells. Stop when the lights flash and before the gate lowers. Driving around or under a closing gate is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. It shows that parking is not allowed in this area.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful where children are present. Always give pedestrians the right of way at crosswalks.

questions.question: When should you slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where pedestrians are present, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking a non-prescription drug?

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medications can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings about cold and allergy medicines. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a freeway?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up if you miss your turn or exit. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: What should you do before driving an unfamiliar vehicle?

options.text: Not put too much thought into it because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Disregard any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes before driving to familiarize yourself with the operation and location of all the vehicle's equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes before driving to familiarize yourself with the operation and location of all the vehicle's equipment.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn are located. Fix any defects before driving.

questions.question: What should you do if you are angry after an incident at work?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
Stop at your favorite bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, cool off before driving. Letting anger control your driving is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: What should you do before starting the engine?

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all of the vehicle's occupants have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all of the vehicle's occupants have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: When are children required to wear seat belts?

options.text: Anytime they are in a moving car.
If their parents think they should.
If they choose to do so.
Only if they weigh under 100 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anytime they are in a moving car.
questions.explanation: Florida law requires all children under 18 to wear fastened seat belts in a moving vehicle, no matter where they sit.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating or drinking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it harder to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is behind you?

options.text: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Get out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact. Speeding up may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter the road or driveway ahead from your direction. Turn around and find a different way.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not pay attention to how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop if a train or another vehicle is using the tracks.

questions.question: When should you drive in a lane showing a red X?

options.text: If there is no visible oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: A red X means that lane is closed. Never drive in a lane with a red X above it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that left turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What must you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, take out the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?
questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can lead to hitting other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What can impair your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired can all impair your driving ability.

questions.question: What documents must you show when stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check?
questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times when driving.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It makes you feel too confident.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and harms your vision. It makes it harder to judge distances and react to what's around you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is coming up.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are around.
Signal only if you see other traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are around.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. This is the law. Don't skip signaling just because you don't see other cars.

questions.question: As you drive, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When a police officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: When you see an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Don't make eye contact. Slow down and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't make eye contact. Slow down and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm around aggressive drivers. Put distance between you and them. Slow down and let them pass. Don't look at them or make hand gestures.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when you think all the kids have left.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a school bus with its stop arm out. Don't drive until the stop arm goes back in.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This regulation sign means U-turns are not allowed. Regulation signs tell drivers what they must and must not do.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no train in sight, you must stop if:
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a posted stop sign, or a flagman signaling you to stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is:
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn drivers about railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is coming and to watch for trains.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you that bicycles may cross here.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Keep driving and use the next exit.
Back up to reach the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make sudden turns to catch a missed exit. Continue driving safely to the next exit.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency responders.

questions.question: This sign shows:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: Before you turn, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop and check for other traffic. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What causes distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus fully on the road. Any extra activity can be dangerous and distracting.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Exit at the next exit and come back.
Roll down your window and ask for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and come back.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on a highway. Go to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react. Keep your eyes moving to avoid focusing on one thing too long.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: These spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are for buses and carpools only.

questions.correctAnswerText: These spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: It is hard to see in the dark.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see in the dark.
questions.explanation: Your vision is limited at night. Use your headlights and drive slow enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: While backing out of your driveway.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, adjust all mirrors so you can see without leaning forward or backward.
